subject: general
question: In which year was The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act introduced in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, also known as the RTE Act, was introduced in the year **2009**.
 
• This Act ensures that every child in India has the right to full-time elementary education of satisfactory and equitable quality in a formal school which satisfies certain essential norms and standards.
 
• The Act makes education a fundamental right for children between the ages of 6 and 14 years and specifies minimum norms in elementary schools.
 
• It requires all private schools to reserve 25% of seats to children from disadvantaged groups and physically challenged children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The RTE Act was passed by the Indian Parliament on **4th August 2009**, and came into effect on **1st April 2010**.
 
• The Act is in consonance with Article 21A of the Indian Constitution, which was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, mandating free and compulsory education for children in the 6-14 age group.
 
• The Act also mandates improvement in the quality of education through proper infrastructure, trained teachers, and comprehensive evaluation systems.
 
• It emphasizes the need for inclusive education, ensuring that children from various socio-economic backgrounds receive equal educational opportunities.
